title: app.del() removed
description: Express 5 no longer supports app.del(). Use app.delete() instead. Also applies to router.del().

detection.note: Search for .del( calls on app or router objects

fix.notes: Also remove any shim like 'router.del = router.delete' — it is no longer needed.

title: app.param(fn) removed
description: The app.param(fn) single-argument signature for modifying app.param behaviour has been removed. Express 5 no longer supports it.

fix.after: // Remove this call entirely; use app.param(name, fn) per-parameter instead
fix.notes: Only the two-argument app.param(name, fn) form is supported.

title: Pluralized method names — req.acceptsCharset / req.acceptsEncoding / req.acceptsLanguage removed
description: req.acceptsCharset(), req.acceptsEncoding(), and req.acceptsLanguage() have been removed. Use the pluralised versions req.acceptsCharsets(), req.acceptsEncodings(), req.acceptsLanguages() instead.

detection.note: Search for the singular (non-plural) versions of these req methods

fix.notes: Simple rename — add an 's' to the end of each method name.

source: Removed methods and properties — Pluralized method names

title: req.param(name) removed
description: req.param(name) has been removed. Look up parameters explicitly in req.params, req.body, or req.query.

detection.note: Search for req.param( calls throughout the codebase

fix.notes: For route params like :id, :field, :level use req.params.<name>. For body params use req.body.<name>. For query params use req.query.<name>.

title: res.json(status, obj) signature removed
description: Express 5 no longer supports res.json(obj, status) or res.json(status, obj). Use res.status(status).json(obj) instead.

detection.note: Search for res.json calls with two arguments where one is a numeric status code or variable

fix.notes: Move the status to res.status() and chain .json().

source: Removed methods and properties — res.json(obj, status)

title: res.redirect('back') removed
description: Express 5 no longer supports the magic string 'back' in res.redirect() and res.location(). Use req.get('Referrer') || '/' instead.

detection.note: Search for res.redirect('back') or res.location('back') calls

fix.notes: Replace the magic string 'back' with an explicit referrer check.

source: Removed methods and properties — res.redirect('back') and res.location('back')

title: res.send(status) with numeric-only argument removed
description: Express 5 no longer supports res.send(status) where status is a number. Use res.sendStatus(statusCode) instead.

detection.note: Search for res.send() calls with a lone numeric argument (status code only)

fix.notes: When the only argument to res.send() is a number, use res.sendStatus() instead.

source: Removed methods and properties — res.send(body, status) and res.send(status)

title: res.sendfile() removed (use res.sendFile())
description: The lowercase res.sendfile() has been replaced by camelCased res.sendFile() in Express 5.
note: No matching call sites found in usage map

title: Wildcard route paths must be named (/* → /*splat)
description: In Express 5, the wildcard * in route paths must have a name. Replace /* with /*splat (or any other name).

detection.note: Search for route path strings containing a bare /* without a name following the *

fix.before:
app.get('/files/*', function (req, res) {
app.all('/api/*', function (req, res) {
fix.after:
app.get('/files/*splat', function (req, res) {
app.all('/api/*splat', function (req, res) {
fix.notes: Any name after * is acceptable. Also update req.params access from req.params[0] to req.params.splat.

title: req.params wildcard values are now arrays
description: In Express 5, wildcard parameters captured via /*name produce an array of path segments, not a single string. req.params[0] is no longer valid.

detection.note: Search for req.params[0] access which relied on the old unnamed wildcard behaviour

fix.notes: After renaming /* to /*splat, access the value as req.params.splat. It will be a string for single-segment matches or an array for multi-segment. Join with '/' if needed: Array.isArray(req.params.splat) ? req.params.splat.join('/') : req.params.splat.

source: Changed — req.params (wildcard parameters are now arrays)

title: req.query is now a read-only getter
description: req.query is no longer a writable property. Assigning to req.query or any of its properties will silently fail or throw. The default query parser has also changed from 'extended' to 'simple'.

detection.note: Search for assignments to req.query or its sub-properties

fix.after:
var status = req.query.status ? req.query.status.toLowerCase() : undefined;
var priority = req.query.priority ? req.query.priority.toLowerCase() : undefined;
fix.notes: Do not mutate req.query. Store derived values in local variables and use those variables downstream in the same handler.

title: res.redirect(url, status) argument order changed
description: Express 5 no longer supports res.redirect(url, status). The new signature is res.redirect(status, url). Calls with a single URL argument (default 302) are unaffected.

detection.note: Search for res.redirect with a numeric status as the second argument

fix.notes: Swap the argument order. Single-argument calls like res.redirect('/dashboard') are unchanged.

source: Removed methods and properties — res.redirect(url, status)

title: Optional route parameter suffix ? removed (use braces)
description: Express 5 path-to-regexp no longer supports the ? suffix for optional route segments (e.g. :param?). Use braces syntax instead: {:param} or :param{:ext}.

detection.note: Search for route path strings containing :paramName? optional param suffix

fix.notes: Wrap the optional segment (including the leading slash) in braces. When the param is absent, req.params.field / req.params.level will be undefined.

source: Changed — Path route matching syntax (optional character ? no longer supported)
